title: Scout by username
acceptance: Given a GitHub username, then the languages they use are detected and open, unassigned issues in matching repositories are listed.
evidence: manual: PR 1 and PR 2, the real GitHub API returned 21 opportunities for a sample user.

title: Repository health score
acceptance: Given activity, maintainer response time to outsiders, a CONTRIBUTING file and whether the issue has an open PR, then a 0 to 100 score is computed with the documented weights (30, 35, 15, 20).

title: AI policy detection
acceptance: Given contributing text, then the policy is classified as forbidden, disclosure, allowed or unknown.

title: Rate limiting and API limits
status: Implemented, not verified end to end
acceptance: Given repeated requests from one client, then requests beyond the limit are rejected; given GitHub rate limiting, then a clear error is shown.
Given a forged X-Forwarded-For, then it does not create a new rate limit bucket.
Given the server token and a private repository, then /api/issue answers 403.
evidence: manual: PR 1, limiter exercised through the route. Unit tests cover the limiter, client key, cache and repo checks. In-memory only, so it resets per server instance.

title: Optional GitHub sign-in
status: Implemented, not verified end to end
acceptance: Given OAuth credentials, when the user signs in, then requests use their token and the API limit rises; the token is stored in an httpOnly cookie.
evidence: manual: implemented in PR 1; awaiting an OAuth App to verify the full round trip.

title: AI plan of attack (bring your own key)
status: Implemented, not verified end to end
acceptance: Given a key, when the user asks for a plan, then the issue is fetched and a summary, difficulty and plan are shown; the key never reaches this app's server.
evidence: manual: PR 1; not run against a real provider.

title: Filtering and sorting
acceptance: Given results, then they can be filtered by AI policy with counts and sorted by score or stars.
evidence: manual: PR 2, filter and sort verified in Chrome with real data.
